answer: Submissions that land within 132 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The haven detector writes to copper, and ember shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 234 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 34 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
